Jove.what: Jove nods to Thetis, promising honour to Achilles, then quarrels with Juno.
Jove sends a lying Dream to Agamemnon promising the fall of Troy.
Jove forbids the gods to interfere, weighs the fates and tips the scales to the Trojans.
Jove is seduced by Juno on Ida and falls asleep.
Jove wakes, threatens Juno and sends Apollo to revive Hector.
Jove decides Hector must be ransomed and sends Thetis and Iris, then Mercury.

Hector.what: Hector goes to Troy, rebukes Paris and takes farewell of Andromache and Astyanax.
Hector challenges the Achaeans and fights Ajax to a draw.
Hector scorns the omen and smashes the gates with a huge stone.
Hector kills Patroclus after Apollo disarms him.
Hector puts on Achilles' armour and fights over Patroclus' body.
Hector flees Achilles three times round Troy, is tricked by Minerva and killed.

Minerva.what: Minerva stops Achilles from drawing his sword on Agamemnon.
Minerva rouses Ulysses to turn the fleeing army back.
Minerva persuades Pandarus to shoot Menelaus and turns the arrow aside.
Minerva inspires Diomed and helps him wound Mars.
Minerva aids Diomed and Ulysses on their night raid.
Minerva, as Deiphobus, tricks Hector into standing against Achilles.

Ajax.what: Ajax, chosen by lot, fights Hector to a draw.
Ajax urges the envoys to leave after Achilles refuses.
Ajax fells Hector with a stone.
Ajax defends the ships, striding the decks with a sea-pike.
Ajax fights to save Patroclus' body and covers the retreat.
Ajax wrestles Ulysses to a draw and fights Diomed to a draw in the games.

Apollo.what: Apollo answers Chryses' prayer and sends a plague on the Achaeans.
Apollo plans the duel with Minerva and raises the fallen Hector.
Apollo revives Hector and tramples the Achaean wall flat.
Apollo strikes down Patroclus and disarms him.
Apollo disguises himself as Agenor and lures Achilles away from Troy.
Apollo reveals himself to Achilles, then abandons Hector.
Apollo rebukes the gods for neglecting Hector and shields his body.

Agamemnon.what: Agamemnon refuses Chryses, quarrels with Achilles and takes Briseis.
Agamemnon believes the Dream and tests the army by urging flight.
Agamemnon laments Menelaus' wound and rallies and rebukes his captains.
Agamemnon proposes flight, then offers Achilles vast gifts.
Agamemnon arms, kills many Trojans, and is wounded by Coon.
Agamemnon reconciles with Achilles, blames Folly, and swears he never touched Briseis.

Achilles.what: Achilles quarrels with Agamemnon, loses Briseis and asks Thetis to help the Trojans.
Achilles refuses the envoys' gifts and speaks of his two fates.
Achilles lets Patroclus wear his armour and prays to Jove for him.
Achilles learns of Patroclus' death, grieves and terrifies the Trojans with his shout.
Achilles ends his anger, mourns, arms, and hears Xanthus foretell his death.
Achilles slaughters Trojans in the river, killing Lycaon and Asteropaeus.
Achilles kills Hector and drags his body behind his chariot.
Achilles weeps with Priam and ransoms Hector's body.

Juno.what: Juno quarrels with Jove on Olympus until Vulcan soothes her.
Juno and Minerva arm and ride to Troy to oppose Mars.
Juno urges Neptune to help the Danaans and is turned back by Iris.
Juno borrows Venus's girdle, enlists Sleep and seduces Jove.
Juno calls on Vulcan to subdue the river Xanthus and beats Diana.

Idomeneus.what: Idomeneus arms, goes to the left wing and kills Othryoneus, Asius and Alcathous.

Menelaus.what: Menelaus fights Alexandrus in single combat and nearly kills him.
Menelaus is wounded by Pandarus and treated by Machaon.
Menelaus kills Euphorbus and defends Patroclus' body.
Menelaus is beaten by Antilochus' trick in the chariot race.

Meriones.what: Meriones fights beside Idomeneus on the left wing.
Meriones helps carry Patroclus' body toward the ships.
Meriones leads the wood-gathering and wins the archery.

Nestor.what: Nestor backs Agamemnon's plan and urges order by tribes.
Nestor recalls killing Ereuthalion and proposes the wall and trench.
Nestor is rescued by Diomed after his horse is hit.
Nestor carries off Machaon and tells Patroclus the Elis raid story.
Nestor rallies the Achaeans at the ships.

Ulysses.what: Ulysses turns the men back, beats Thersites and addresses the assembly.
Ulysses pleads with Achilles on Agamemnon's behalf.
Ulysses and Diomed kill Dolon and take Rhesus' horses.
Ulysses rebukes Agamemnon's proposal to launch the ships.
Ulysses insists the army eat before battle.
Ulysses wrestles Ajax to a draw and wins the foot-race.

Diomed.what: Diomed rages in battle, wounds Aeneas, Venus and Mars.
Diomed discovers the guest-friendship with Glaucus and swaps armour.
Diomed saves Nestor until Jove's thunderbolt turns him back.
Diomed rebukes Agamemnon's flight and rallies the council.
Diomed and Ulysses spy, kill Dolon and slaughter the Thracians.

Patroclus.what: Patroclus tends the wounded Eurypylus after hearing Nestor.
Patroclus begs Achilles for his armour and routs the Trojans.
Patroclus kills Sarpedon, then is struck down by Apollo, Euphorbus and Hector.
Patroclus' ghost appears to Achilles asking for burial.

Aeneas.what: Aeneas is felled by Diomed's stone and rescued by Venus and Apollo.
Aeneas duels Achilles and is saved by Neptune.

Paris.what: Paris fights Menelaus and is rescued by Venus.
Hector rebukes Paris, who then rejoins him for battle.
Paris refuses to return Helen at the Trojan council.
Paris wounds Diomed, Machaon and Eurypylus with arrows.

Priam.what: Priam watches the oaths sworn and Helen names the Achaean heroes.
Priam begs Hector to come inside the walls and cries out in grief.
Priam goes to Achilles, supplicates him and ransoms Hector's body.

Antilochus.what: Antilochus brings Achilles the news of Patroclus' death.
Antilochus beats Menelaus by a trick in the chariot race.

Mars.what: Mars aids the Trojans and is wounded by Diomed with Minerva's help.
Mars arms to avenge Ascalaphus but Minerva disarms him.
Mars fights for Troy and is felled by Minerva.

Neptune.what: Neptune complains to Jove about the Achaean wall.
Neptune secretly rouses the Achaeans and fights beside Idomeneus.
Neptune protests Jove's order, then yields and leaves the field.

Iris.what: Iris turns Juno and Minerva back with Jove's threat.
Iris orders Neptune out of the battle.
Iris tells Achilles to show himself at the trench.
Iris fetches the winds to light Patroclus' pyre.
Iris fetches Thetis and tells Priam to ransom Hector.

Venus.what: Venus rescues Paris and forces Helen to his bed.
Venus is wounded by Diomed while rescuing Aeneas.

Polydamas.what: Polydamas reads the eagle and snake omen and urges caution.
Polydamas urges retreat into Troy; Hector refuses.

Thetis.what: Thetis hears Achilles and supplicates Jove for him.
Thetis comforts Achilles and gets armour from Vulcan.
Thetis brings Vulcan's armour to Achilles.
Thetis relays Jove's command and persuades Achilles to accept ransom.

Agenor.what: Agenor stands against Achilles and is rescued by Apollo.

Glaucus.what: Glaucus meets Diomed and exchanges armour with him.
Glaucus is wounded by Ajax and Teucer.
Glaucus rebukes Hector over Sarpedon's body.

Vulcan.what: Vulcan soothes Juno and restores peace on Olympus.
Vulcan forges Achilles' armour and shield.
Vulcan's fire subdues the river Xanthus.

Sarpedon.what: Sarpedon rebukes Hector and fights Tlepolemus.
Sarpedon speaks to Glaucus and tears a breach in the wall.

Diana.what: Diana is beaten by Juno and complains to Jove.

Automedon.what: Automedon drives in the chariot race.

Sthenelus.what: Sthenelus pulls the arrow from Diomed and drives his chariot.

Teucer.what: Teucer shoots many Trojans until Hector stones him.
Teucer helps Ajax at the wall.
Teucer's bowstring is broken by Jove.

Thoas.what: Thoas advises a rearguard stand at the wall.

Ajax son of Oileus.what: Ajax son of Oileus is inspired by Neptune and holds the line.
Ajax son of Oileus kills the most fleeing Trojans.

Antenor.what: Antenor urges the Trojans to return Helen.

Eurypylus.what: Eurypylus is wounded by Paris and tended by Patroclus.

Helen.what: Helen names the Achaean heroes for Priam, then is forced to Paris' bed.
Helen blames herself when Hector visits.

Helenus.what: Helenus sends Hector to Troy to have the women pray to Minerva.
Helenus urges Hector to challenge the Achaeans.

Andromache.what: Andromache begs Hector to stay at the Scaean gates.
Andromache hears the cries, faints on the wall and mourns Hector.
Andromache laments Hector at his funeral.

Briseis.what: Briseis is taken from Achilles' tent by Agamemnon's heralds.
Briseis is returned and laments Patroclus.

Mercury.what: Mercury guides Priam to Achilles' tent and wakes him to leave.

Idaeus.what: Idaeus drives Priam to Achilles' camp with Hector's ransom.

Phoenix.what: Phoenix tells his own story and urges Achilles to yield.

Xanthus.what: Xanthus the horse speaks and foretells Achilles' death.
The river Xanthus attacks Achilles and is subdued by Vulcan.

Calchas.what: Calchas names the cause of the plague, provoking the quarrel between Agamemnon and Achilles.

Hecuba.what: Hecuba gathers the matrons and brings a robe to Minerva's temple.
Hecuba begs Hector from the wall to come inside, but he stands firm.
Hecuba begs Priam not to go to Achilles, then laments Hector's death.

Machaon.what: Machaon is fetched and treats Menelaus's wound.
Machaon is wounded by Paris and carried off by Nestor.

Pandarus.what: Persuaded by Minerva, Pandarus shoots Menelaus and breaks the truce.
Pandarus wounds Diomed, then is killed by him.

Pisander.what: Pisander is killed by Agamemnon during his rampage.

Alcathous.what: Alcathous, Anchises's son-in-law, is killed by Idomeneus.

Alcimus.what: Alcimus, Achilles' squire, attends as Priam supplicates Achilles.

Antiphus.what: Antiphus is killed by Agamemnon during his rampage.

Asius.what: Asius drives his chariot to the gates and is repelled by the Lapithae.

Asteropaeus.what: Asteropaeus wounds Achilles slightly but is killed by him.

Astyanax.what: Astyanax is frightened by Hector's helmet as Hector prays for him.

Boreas.what: Boreas comes with Zephyrus at Achilles' prayer and blows the pyre alight.

Euphorbus.what: Euphorbus first wounds Patroclus, before Hector kills him.

Euryalus.what: Euryalus is knocked out by Epeus in the boxing.

Hecamede.what: Hecamede serves a mixed drink in Nestor's tent.

Hippolochus.what: Hippolochus is killed by Agamemnon during his rampage.

Hippothous.what: Hippothous is killed by Ajax in the struggle over Patroclus's body.

Leonteus.what: Leonteus holds the gate with Polypoetes and kills many Trojans.

Lycaon.what: Lycaon begs Achilles for mercy but is killed and thrown into the river.

Polydorus.what: Polydorus, Priam's youngest son, falls, provoking Hector to attack Achilles.

Polypoetes.what: Polypoetes holds the gate with Leonteus against Asius's attack.
Polypoetes wins the quoit throw at the funeral games.

Simois.what: Simois is called by Xanthus to help flood Achilles.

Theano.what: Theano prays to Minerva in her temple, but the goddess refuses.

Themis.what: Themis summons the gods to council at Jove's order.

Tlepolemus.what: Tlepolemus fights Sarpedon and is killed.

Alastor.what: Alastor carries the stoned Teucer away from the field to the ships.

Antea.what: Antea slanders Bellerophon, who is sent to Lycia with a deadly letter.

Bellerophon.what: Bellerophon survives the Chimaera, Solymi, Amazons and an ambush, and marries the king's daughter.

Charis.what: Charis welcomes Thetis into Vulcan's house.

Chryseis.what: Chryseis is taken by Ulysses and restored to her father Chryses.

Chryses.what: Chryses is refused ransom by Agamemnon and prays to Apollo for a plague.
Chryses receives his daughter Chryseis back from Ulysses and sacrifices to Apollo.

Coon.what: Coon wounds Agamemnon, who then kills him and leaves the field.

Dione.what: Dione comforts her wounded daughter Venus on Olympus with tales of gods hurt by mortals.

Discord.what: Discord is sent by Jove to the ships and rouses the Achaeans to battle.

Dolon.what: Dolon volunteers to spy on the Achaeans in return for Achilles' horses.
Dolon is captured by Ulysses and Diomed, reveals the Trojan camp, and is killed by Diomed.

Dream.what: Dream, sent by Jove in Nestor's likeness, tells Agamemnon he will take Troy.

Eniopeus.what: Eniopeus, Hector's charioteer, is killed by Diomed.

Epeus.what: Epeus knocks out Euryalus in the boxing match and wins the prize.

Eumelus.what: Eumelus' chariot is wrecked in the race, and Achilles consoles him.

Folly.what: Folly, Jove's daughter, is flung from heaven by Jove in Agamemnon's tale.

Imbrius.what: Imbrius is killed by Teucer, and the Ajaxes seize his body.

Melanippus.what: Melanippus is killed by Antilochus in the fighting at the ships.

Meleager.what: Meleager withdraws in anger from the Calydonian war and yields too late, in Phoenix's tale.

Myrmidons.what: The Myrmidons shrink from Vulcan's armour as Thetis brings it to Achilles.

Nereids.what: The Nereids rise from the sea with Thetis to comfort the grieving Achilles.

Night.what: Night protects Sleep from Jove's wrath, as Sleep recalls to Juno.

Paeeon.what: Paeeon heals Mars on Olympus after Jove rebukes him.

Rhesus.what: Rhesus, Thracian king, is killed by Diomed in his sleep and Ulysses takes his horses.

Sleep.what: Sleep agrees to help Juno, lulls Jove on Ida and tells Neptune Jove sleeps.

Thersites.what: Thersites abuses Agamemnon and urges departure, and Ulysses thrashes him.

Zephyrus.what: Zephyrus, called by Iris, blows with Boreas all night to light Patroclus' pyre.
